lesson_title: 15 vs 25: The Loan That Costs 20x More
hook_text: Bank: 15%. Mashonisa: 25%. Sounds close? One is TWENTY times more expensive.
clip_script: Two people offer to lend you R4 000. The bank says 15 percent. The mashonisa says 25. Read the small print out loud: the bank's is 15 percent per year. The mashonisa's is 25 percent per month. The bank's rent for a whole year: R600. The mashonisa's rent for one month: R1 000. In his first month you pay more than the bank asks for a whole year. Three months in, you have paid R3 000 — and if you were only paying interest, the R4 000 is still owed in full. Stretch his rate to a year: 25 times 12 is 300 percent, against the bank's 15. Never compare two rates until they wear the same time period.
visual_style: Split screen: calm bank teller stacking R600 once, versus a growing monthly pile of R1 000 notes that towers over it, with the per-year and per-month labels flashing red.
pacing: Slow trap setup, rapid-fire monthly charges stacking, hard-stop rule at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — grow savings and spot bad loans, no formulae needed.
